narrative: In this stylized demo—which is not an engineering estimate—a magnitude 7.2 earthquake coupled with a 13.06-foot MLLW king tide and storm surge initiates a cascade at the Perimeter Seawall. Seawall breaches directly compromise electric substations, fuel handling, and transport links. Substation loss then propagates failure to the communications hub and high-pressure water pumps, while degraded fuel, communications, and bridge approaches compound to sever the ferry terminal and evacuation roads. The 1-in-100 tail ($1,175M VaR99) is driven by systemic collapse when initial seawall and substation failures trigger near-total loss of downstream fire suppression and evacuation capacity. Proposed fixes break this chain by hardening the seawall against liquefaction and overtopping, isolating and islanding substations, and adding localized redundancies like backup power, flexible couplings, and autonomous failovers across downstream nodes.
